reason: I bill cost-plus, so $1,500 either comes out of my margin or I have to talk the homeowner into a new line item, and most of my clients already have architect drawings they're happy with. With only a few homes a year I don't have a pile of jobs where nobody is producing 3D.
objection: Is $1,500 a home worth it on our margins? If the homeowner won't pay for the line item I'm eating it, and I can't tell that a walkthrough saves me change orders or wins me a job.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing the free first build on one of my real plans and having a homeowner say they'd happily pay for it as a pre-construction line, or proof that it cuts change orders enough to cover the cost.
